```{r}
#| label: library
#| include: false
options(housepi.footer.sample = TRUE)
library(housepi)
housepi_theme_set()
set.seed(42)
```

Contact risks allow modelling differential transmission between groups of individuals within a household.
Unlike group risks, which apply to a single individual, contact risks define pairwise from/to relationships.
Like group risks, they are absolute: each pair gets its own transmission rate, unless a reference pair is chosen for the others to multiply.
We illustrate the API using the Matsumoto influenza household survey.

# Define a contact risk

We start by loading the final-size model and the `flu_2014_matsumoto` dataset.
This dataset contains household reports of influenza episodes with a `member` column distinguishing different household member categories. 
To simplify this walkthrough, we consider only two categories: "child" and "adult":

```{r}
#| label: load-model-data
# simplify 
dataset <- flu_2014_matsumoto |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    member = dplyr::case_when(
      member == "student" ~ "child",
      member == "sibling" ~ "child",
      .default = "adult"
    )
  )

# inspect the data
head(dataset)

# define a final-size model and load parameter template
hhmodel <- dataset |>
  new_housepi_model("final-size") |>
  add_parameter(import = "template")
```

Use `add_contact_risk()` to define pairwise transmission rates based on a categorical covariate.
This creates from/to parameter pairs for each combination of groups.

```{r}
#| label: add-contact-risk
# define symmetric contact risks automatically
hhmodel |>
  add_contact_risk("member") |>
  get_contact_risks()

# asymmetric case
hhmodel |>
  add_contact_risk("member", symmetric = FALSE) |>
  get_contact_risks()
```

Each row in the output represents a directed from/to pair.
The `param_name` column gives the corresponding parameter that will scale the transmission rate between those groups.
If not stated differently, the contact is assumed symmetric, which implies that pairs from/to and to/from share the same parameter.
Parameters generated by the contact risk follow the same MCMC defaults as in group risks.
Their shared MCMC definition can be provided as shown in [Group risks](group_risks.html).

# Specify a reference pair

The `.reference` pair is fixed at 1, and every other parameter is read against it.
Provide a `reference` to select which from/to pair acts as the baseline,
or ask for `".auto"` to take the most frequent combination:

```{r}
#| label: custom-reference
hhmodel |>
  add_contact_risk(
    by = "member",
    reference = c(from_member = "child", to_member = "child")
  ) |>
  get_contact_risks()
```

A convenience shorthand applies the same reference value to both from and to:
e.g. passing `reference = c(member = "child")` is equivalent to the previous.
